item.title: The Number of Cluster Munition Victims Is Growing
item.description: Despite an international ban on the use of cluster munitions, the number of people they killed or wounded soared last year, mainly due to their use in the Russia-Ukraine war. Cluster munitions are bombs that indiscriminately launch scores of explosive submunitions. Many of them fail to detonate on impact, turning vast tracts of land into ... Read more

item.title: COP31 enters decisive week as climate talks face political test and AI initiatives gather pace
item.description: New international initiatives on artificial intelligence and green industrialization showcased technology's growing role in climate action, even as negotiators remained deadlocked on finance, fossil fuels and adaptation ahead of the final stretch of talks.

item.title: Funding cuts raise risks of trafficking and exploitation for refugee children
item.description: Sharp reductions in humanitarian funding are putting refugees, particularly children, at increased risk of being trafficked, exploited or abused, while the systems that protect them are weakening.

item.title: Guterres calls for a legally binding instrument for ‘killer robots'
item.description: Talks began in Geneva on Monday to push for controls on lethal autonomous weapons systems that are often referred to as “killer robots”.

item.title: At his final ASEAN Summit, Guterres upholds cooperation and action on Myanmar
item.description: UN Secretary-General António Guterres underscored the need for stronger collaboration with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and an end to the crisis in Myanmar, in remarks to regional leaders meeting in the Philippine capital Manila on Monday.

item.title: ‘Peace begins in our hearts’: Children close Muscat forum with a message to the world
item.description: Children from across the world sent a message of peace from the Omani capital Muscat on Monday, calling for an end to hatred, respect for diversity and the protection of human rights.

item.title: ‘An unfulfilled plan helps no one’: Superbug plans have doubled, but few countries are delivering
item.description: More countries are drawing up plans to tackle antimicrobial resistance (AMR), but major gaps in testing and treatment mean billions of people continue to be at risk, according to new data released by the World Health Organization (WHO) on Monday.

item.title: Lebanon leading the way in mental health support
item.description: Mental health support must be a core part of the humanitarian response, said the UN Deputy Secretary-General during a visit to Lebanon over the weekend, where efforts to address the psychological toll of years of conflict and instability offer valuable lessons for other crisis-affected countries.

item.title: AI gets climate science right – until users push back
item.description: The best AI models answer most climate science questions correctly, but they often abandon established facts as soon as a user disagrees, according to a new report co-authored by the UN.

item.title: Syria: Progress ‘real’ but fragile, as remnants of war wreck young lives
item.description: Syria is showing “undeniable signs of progress” nearly two years after the fall of the Assad regime, but explosive ordnance, the approaching winter and severe funding shortfalls threaten those fragile gains, senior UN officials told the Security Council on Monday.

item.title: The Legal Path to Autocracy
item.description: Zimbabwe’s President Emmerson Mnangagwa, who took over when a miliary coup ended Robert Mugabe’s 37 years in power, has made clear he has no intention of limiting himself to a decade at the top. item.title: Africa Makes Some Gains but Faces Major Setbacks at COP31
item.description: Today (November 15) marks the second week of negotiations at the United Nations climate summit in the resort city of Antalya, Turkey. item.title: Time to Home
item.description: After a flood or other disaster, finding a safe home can take years. At COP31, we should commit to measuring – and shortening – that wait.
